text.p: The following are the main stories from Tuesday morning's German newspapers:
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG
- More and more Germans spending holidays at home as money gets tighter
- German share and bond markets hit new record levels
- Privatisation agency sets aside 250 million marks to help small and medium sized privatised firms in east Germany
- Concentration in food retail sector puts brand-name manufacturers under pressure
HANDELSBLATT
- Mannesmann and France's Vallourec to cooperate on seamless steel pipes
- Critical shareholder Wenger fails in suit against Deutsche Bank
- Dollar stabilises after G7 meeting
- Lack of money forced Germans to cut back on travel
- Cabinet decision on Eurofighter said to be postponed
- Berlin firms unusually reluctant to innovate
- Grundig goes on the offensive, says it has resources to survive well into next century
- Cartel Office bans Herlitz takeover of Landre GmbH
SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG
- Building workers to get no unemployment benefit during winter layoff
- Court says East Germany was not fully sovereign to decide on its own border policing regime
- State of Schleswig-Holstein applies to sell cannabis in limited form via chemist's shops
- German architects say restoration and repair is the way to boost construction industry in coming years
- Australia interested in buying high-speed Transrapid train, Thyssen boss says
- Cabinet decision on Eurofighter said to be postponed
DIE WELT
- Pressure grows on Chancellor Kohl to decide by April whether he will stand in next election
- IG Metall engineering union welcomes individual wage arrangements in eastern German firms in difficulty
- East German states want new approach to economic assistance
- Grundig sees way out of its crisis
- Dollar remains in demand despite G7 declaration
